results.summary_before: This project provides a bridge between an RP2040 microcontroller and a Tiny Tapeout chip using SPI. It is designed for educational purposes and demonstrates how to interface a microcontroller with custom hardware. The design includes memory-mapped registers and is tested by sending commands over SPI. It is notable for enabling easy control of Tiny Tapeout projects from an RP2040.
results.summary: This project is a Tiny Tapeout demo competition entry that generates VGA video and audio output. It includes a logo, star field, floating point unit, synthesizer, and sequencer. The video output is VGA 640x480 at 60 Hz, clocked at 50.4 MHz with two clock cycles per pixel. It is tested using a TinyVGA Pmod and an audio Pmod.

results.summary_before: This project uses a 16-bit LFSR to generate pseudo-random tones. It is designed to demonstrate the use of an LFSR for sound generation. The output is a square wave whose frequency is controlled by the LFSR state. It is tested by connecting an audio output and listening to the generated tones.
results.summary: This project is a test for an 8b10 serdes containing an 8b10 encoder and decoder. It accepts 9-bit symbols and outputs the encoded or decoded results after a number of clock cycles. The design uses a manual clock divided by 10 to generate internal clocks and supports an optional scrambler. Testing involves sending characters and verifying the received data matches the transmitted data.

results.summary_before: This design generates a VGA video signal that animates columns of pink hearts transitioning on and off the screen. It is implemented in Verilog using the VGA Playground environment and is intended to be tested by running the simulation and observing the output. The design requires a VGA monitor connected to the Tiny VGA PMOD pinout. The project is a playful visual demonstration rather than a practical application.
results.summary: This project is a stochastic music generator that uses two Markov chains to select note and duration on a pentatonic scale. It features a 16-bit LFSR entropy source, adjustable BPM, and selectable probability matrices. The logic control module uses two FSMs to model the Markov chains and drive a PWM generator. It is tested by connecting a buzzer PMOD and changing the seed and control inputs.

results.summary: This project implements an ECG front end for measuring electrocardiogram signals using a folded cascode based architecture. It has analog input pins INp and INm for the ECG signal, and output pins OUT and OUTDRL. The ref and Vref pins should be biased at 0.9V or connected to an offset compensation circuit. Testing involves connecting electrodes and observing the output with an oscilloscope.

results.summary_before: This project is a VGA 640x480 @ 60 Hz display controller that outputs a 1-bit sigma-delta modulated audio signal. It generates a test pattern on the VGA output and produces a simple tone through the audio output. The design is intended for testing VGA and audio interfaces. results.summary: This project implements a 9-channel oscillator frequency measurement ASIC with programmable gate time, SPI-controlled DAC outputs, and SPI-based ADC sampling. It is controlled over I2C and counts each oscillator input over a programmable time window derived from the 50 MHz system clock. The counts are latched into a snapshot register bank accessible via I2C. Testing involves applying a clock, configuring the gate time, and reading back the measured counts.

results.summary_before: The Lambda Clock is a highly-optimized full digital calendar and clock built for a 10-digit 7-segment multiplexed display architecture using three cascaded 74HC595 shift registers. It includes a BCD-native limit handling to avoid binary-to-BCD resource explosion. The design features a buzzer output and is controlled via a finite state machine. It is notable for its efficient BCD-based timekeeping and display driving.
results.summary: This project is an analog PLL targeted for 2.4 GHz output, with a bandgap reference circuit for the charge pump component. It has analog pins REF_FREQ and OUT_FREQ. Testing involves connecting OUT_FREQ to a multimeter and REF_FREQ to a 20 MHz signal, then observing the output converge to 2.4 GHz within 3 us. The documentation notes that the output frequency may not reach 2.4 GHz and the input frequency may need to be increased.
